title: Loop back: the whole course, working as one
idea: LOOP (review), capstone: no new concept. Celebrate and consolidate the full Laps 0-6 toolkit, mixing every pattern one last time to close the lap.

exercises.prompt: In ONE sentence, what have Laps 0-6 given you?
options: A full toolkit - variables, math, decisions, loops, lists, functions - and the skill to weave them into solutions
exercises.explanation: You can store, compute, decide, repeat, collect, and reuse - and combine all of it to solve real, multi-part problems.

exercises.prompt: Final review: match each pattern to its tell-tale problem phrase.

pairs.right: Is there any / find the first

exercises.explanation: Each phrase points to a pattern. Hearing the phrase and reaching for the pattern is the heart of solving unseen problems.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output (accumulate + helper):

def square(n):
    return n * n

total = 0
for x in [2, 3]:
    total = total + square(x)
print(total)
exercises.explanation: square(2)=4, square(3)=9, total = 13. A helper feeding an accumulator - a weave you can now read on sight.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output (track maximum by hand):

best = nums[0]
nums = [4, 9, 2, 9, 5]
for n in nums:
    if n > best:
        best = n
print(best)
options: This crashes - nums is used before it is defined
exercises.explanation: Order matters: nums[0] is read before nums exists, so this errors. A reminder that lines run top to bottom - a Lap 0 truth that never stops mattering.

exercises.prompt:
Fixed version of the above (nums defined first). Now what prints?

nums = [4, 9, 2, 9, 5]
best = nums[0]
for n in nums:
    if n > best:
        best = n
print(best)
exercises.explanation: With the order fixed, best tracks up to 9 (the first 9 wins; the second ties and > does not replace it). Track-the-maximum, built by hand.
11, 8, and 20 are at least 8, so kept = 3. A filter expressed as a count-with-condition.

exercises.prompt: Order the universal problem-solving spine one last time.
blocks: Plan: split into parts, choose a pattern for each
Check: re-run the example and a fresh one
exercises.explanation: Understand, Example, Plan, Code, Check. This spine carried you through every guided problem and works on anything new.

exercises.prompt: This unit, and all of Lap 6, introduced zero brand-new syntax.
exercises.explanation: Lap 6 was about combining and consolidating. Every piece was already yours - the growth was in weaving them confidently.

exercises.prompt: Review (no-builtin rule, one last time): to total a list, you should...
options: Build a running sum with a loop and an accumulator
exercises.explanation: You build totals, biggests, counts, and filters yourself with loops - that understanding is the whole point, and builtins like sum/max are never used.

exercises.prompt: You have finished Lap 6. What can you now do?
options: Take an unseen multi-part problem and solve it end-to-end by recombining everything you have learned
Only solve the exact problems you were shown
Only use one tool at a time
Only predict output, never write code
exercises.explanation: You can read a fresh problem, decompose it, pick patterns, weave them, and prove it works. That is real programming - congratulations on closing the lap!
